extracted.intended_audience: researchers/authors preparing preprint submissions to arXiv
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and mandatory requirements for preparing and submitting research articles (preprints) to the arXiv repository, including acceptable file formats, metadata, filenames, timing/announcement rules, and responsibilities of authors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registered submitters only
rubrics_metrics.description: We accept submissions only from registered authors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions must originate from the author's registered account (see also 'Take responsibility' / third-party submission guidance).

rubrics_metrics.name: License to distribute required
rubrics_metrics.description: Submitters must grant arXiv.org a non-exclusive and irrevocable license to distribute or certify that the work is available under another license that conveys these rights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a mandatory condition of submission; provide a compatible license or grant the stated license to arXiv.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accepted text formats (order of preference)
rubrics_metrics.description: Your submission to the archive must be in one of the following formats (listed in order of preference): (La)TeX, AMS(La)TeX, PDFLaTeX; PDF; PostScript; HTML with JPEG/PNG/GIF images.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: TeX/LaTeX is preferred because it is open and does not hide information. Users of word processors should save as PDF and submit that. Do not submit scanned documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not submit dvi/PS/PDF created from TeX/LaTeX source
rubrics_metrics.description: arXiv will not accept dvi, PS, or PDF created from TeX/LaTeX source.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If submitting TeX/LaTeX source, provide source or use PDFLaTeX workflow rather than uploading derivative DVI/PS/PDF files created from TeX.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scanned documents prohibited
rubrics_metrics.description: We will not accept scanned documents, regardless of format.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scanned PDFs or images of pages are not acceptable as submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Figure file formats allowed
rubrics_metrics.description: Figures for a submission can be in a number of common formats including PostScript (PS/EPS), JPEG (ideal for photographic images), GIF or PNG (best for non-photographic images/bitmaps). PDF figures are allowed only with PDFLaTeX.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use PS/EPS for line drawings/plots; JPEG for photos; GIF/PNG for bitmaps. PDF figures must be used only when compiling with PDFLaTeX.

rubrics_metrics.name: Figure size and downloadability
rubrics_metrics.description: If figure files are too large, readers with poor network connections will not be able to download them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include large figures if necessary but make all possible efforts to reduce their size. See arXiv information on submission sizes and bitmapping help. If you have problems with a large submission, contact arXiv administrators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not omit figures/tables/sections; no abstract-only submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Please note that we do not accept submissions with omitted figures, tables or sections. We also do not accept 'abstract only' submissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Omitted elements (even if linked from another server) are not acceptable; such submissions are unhelpful to readers and of limited archival value.

rubrics_metrics.name: If using LaTeX, include figures via standard macro packages
rubrics_metrics.description: If you submit figures with your (La)TeX source, use standard macro packages (e.g., the graphics and graphicx packages) so that the figures will appear in the document.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: arXiv administration cannot provide help with TeX-related issues; seek help from colleagues for TeX problems.

rubrics_metrics.name: File name character restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: arXiv will accept only the following characters in file names: a-z A-Z 0-9 _ + - . , =. Presence of any other character (e.g. spaces, question marks, asterisks, etc.) will cause the system to reject the file upload or submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These restrictions ensure portability and minimize archival risk; remove or replace disallowed characters before upload.

rubrics_metrics.name: File name case sensitivity and internal references must match
rubrics_metrics.description: File names and extensions are case sensitive on our system. The file names Figure1.PDF and figure1.pdf are not the same.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Whether your local system is case sensitive or not, ensure that internal file references (e.g., LaTeX \\includegraphics commands) match case exactly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limited facilities for data and ancillary files
rubrics_metrics.description: There are limited facilities for including data sets and ancillary files (data, programs, etc.) which are associated with articles submitted to arXiv.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See separate instructions about including data sets and ancillary files for details and restrictions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prepare title/abstract metadata separately
rubrics_metrics.description: See separate instructions on the preparation of separate title/abstract information. This information is used on the abstract pages, in announcements, in RSS feeds, and to support searching.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the separate title/abstract preparation guidance to ensure accurate discoverability and announcement content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Check submission and read arXiv messages before final submit
rubrics_metrics.description: Before you make the final 'Submit Article' step be sure to check carefully both the title/abstract (metadata) and the processed files. If you see any errors or are unhappy with the formatting then correct them or contact arXiv administrators if there are problems you cannot resolve.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify metadata and processed files in the submission preview; use contact channels for unresolved problems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unsubmit before announcement to modify
rubrics_metrics.description: If you discover an error after submission but before public announcement then select the Unsubmit icon next to the submission on your user page to return it to the incomplete status allowing modification and later resubmission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unsubmitting takes the article out of the processing queue and announcement will be scheduled based on the later resubmission time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing and announcement schedule
rubrics_metrics.description: Each day's submissions before 16:00 US Eastern time (EDT/EST) Monday through Friday are not made available to the general public until 20:00 US Eastern time (EDT/EST) Sunday through Thursday. Submissions are normally announced on a daily schedule with no activity on weekends.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: a submission made Monday before 16:00 will be publicly available after 20:00 that day and appear in Tuesday AM mailings; submissions made Friday before 16:00 will be available after 20:00 Sunday, etc.

rubrics_metrics.name: Announcement order and effect of edits
rubrics_metrics.description: Submissions are assigned identifiers and appear in the listings in order based on the submission time (the last time the 'Submit' button was selected). An edit and subsequent 'Submit' will reset this time and change position in the listings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Edits are permitted between 16:00 and the 20:00 announcement time, but doing this will remove the submission from that day's announcements and delay it until the next day. Policy change 2010-03 affects announcement order and effect of edits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Edits before announcement do not create extra versions
rubrics_metrics.description: Edits before an article is publicly announced will not generate additional versions. The date stamp associated with the submission will be the time that the final 'Submit Article' step is completed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not make a new submission for a corrected article or erratum; replace the original submission instead.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authors must submit their own work (take responsibility)
rubrics_metrics.description: Because putting articles on arXiv entails certain responsibilities, authors must make their own submissions. Third-party submissions (by secretaries for example) are often the ones that cause the most problems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There are special instructions for third party submission and index submissions for conference proceedings—consult those if third parties are involved, but authors are expected to take responsibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide institutional affiliation and report numbers
rubrics_metrics.description: The following information is also required for submission: Institutional affiliation for the author(s) must be provided. Official report number(s) from the author(s) institution(s) must be provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include accurate affiliations and report numbers in the metadata as part of submission requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to start a submission
rubrics_metrics.description: To submit an article, use the Submit form or select 'START NEW SUBMISSION' from your user page.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the web submission interface; the final 'Submit' button determines submission timestamp and announcement order.
